# narrow-key

- Dialects: mysql, postgres
- Default: on

## Why

A single-column integer primary key or foreign key narrower than 64 bits runs out of values: 2^31 for a 32-bit key, far fewer for 8, 16 or 24 bits. Widening a key later rewrites the table and every table that references it, under a long lock. Composite keys are not checked; their space is the product of their columns.

## Fix

Declare the key field as a 64-bit integer in the model (bigint, int64) on the primary key and on every foreign key that references it, then regenerate the schema.

## Exception

A small, bounded lookup table (statuses, countries) whose row count can never approach the limit, and the references to it.

The same text is printed by `schemalens explain narrow-key`. An exclusion needs a written reason. Back to the [rule index](README.md).
